title: waker-capabilities v1
description: What one waker says it can do, as data: wakers/<name>/capabilities.json. A waker tells the wake watcher which sessions there are, what state each is in (unread mail, idle, input box empty, mid-turn), and rings one session's doorbell; it posts nothing and decides nothing (wakers/Port.ps1). Each capability is declared in the one vocabulary the host, transport and messenger capability files use - yes, no, declined or unverified - with its evidence; unverified counts as no, and a capability is yes only with evidence that was run. declined means the waker chooses not to offer it: the in-process test waker declares reach.unseen declined so that no production path can pick it. The list is closed: a waker declares every one, and nothing else.

nudge.pointer-only.description: The nudge types one fixed pointer line - the same line whatever the mail says - and never any part of a message body, so no body can sit unsent in an input box or be cut at a newline.

state.box.description: It can read whether a session's input box is empty. A waker without it may only answer boxEmpty unknown, and the watcher never nudges on unknown.

state.turn.description: It can read whether a session is in the middle of a turn. A waker without it may only answer midTurn unknown.

reach.unseen.description: It can nudge a session that has not taken a turn since every session was restored, which is when no session's own side is running to be handed anything.

evidence.description: What was run or read, and when. Never blank.
